svg.title: BHSM Scale Atlas — From core to cosmos
svg.desc: A separate dotted electric-charge circuit starts at the Standard Model slice. Coral positive threads connect up, charm and top quarks. Blue negative threads connect down, strange and bottom quarks plus electron, muon and tau. Neutrinos have no electric-thread connection. Higher slices show positive and negative charged constituents or plasma carriers, without assigning net charge to neutral atoms, molecules or larger objects. No charge is assigned to the core or modes. Molecular handedness and electric sign are distinct. Shared W-plus and W-minus charges are noted in the legend; photon, gluon, Z and Higgs are electrically neutral.

A static public museum poster. Read seven exploded slices from the bottom: proposed hypersphere core; excitations and moire-like modes; the Standard Model of fundamental particles; the periodic table; molecules; planets and stars; the cosmic scale. Three conceptual family paths pass through modes and the I, II and III Standard Model slots. Only the first-generation constituent route continues into ordinary stable atoms; the second and third routes stop before the atomic slice. This excludes exotic atoms and does not remove neutrinos. A neutral fork then reaches a left/right molecular mirror pair. Molecular handedness is a different level of organization, not a conversion of particle generation or particle chirality, and not all molecules are chiral. The lower two slices express the BHSM proposal. A conventional Standard Model particle chart groups six quarks, six leptons, gauge bosons and the Higgs. This is a conceptual scale map, not measured nested shells, a timeline, or a completed derivation from geometry.

g.text: Seven scales of organization. One invitation to explore.
The Standard Model is one slice of the wider BHSM conceptual picture.
READ UPWARD · INCREASING SCALE OF ORGANIZATION
Galaxies, clusters and the cosmic web.
Worlds, stellar systems and their histories.
Bonds, chemistry and possible molecular handedness.
Quarks, leptons, interaction bosons and Higgs.
Overlapping excitations; an analogy for mode structure.
BHSM proposal · no ordinary distance or time in the core
Path key · I/II/III = fermion generations; dashed segments = conditional BHSM family map.
I supplies ordinary atomic constituents; II/III stop here. Neutrinos and exotic atoms are not erased.
The molecular fork shows possible mirror arrangements, not particle chirality. Not all molecules are chiral.
Left/right are visual labels, not R/S or D/L. Slices are conceptual, not measured shells or a timeline.
Electric charge · coral +: u/c/t (+⅔e); blue −: d/s/b (−⅓e), e/μ/τ (−1e).
Neutrinos, photon, gluon, Z and Higgs have zero electric charge and are skipped. W± carry ±1e.
Higher markers show nuclei/electrons and charged matter or plasma; whole objects may be neutral.
No core or mode charge is assigned. Molecular left/right is not electric charge or particle chirality.
Charge and family paths organize the picture; they are not a derived history of individual particles.
Quarks and leptons: spin ½. Antiparticles and gluon color states are not separately tiled.
Gravity is outside the Standard Model; neutrino masses require an extension of its minimal form.
Chirality reference: IUPAC Gold Book · goldbook.iupac.org/terms/view/C01058 and E02069
